page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-360 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors providing 180 physical cores and 360 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance includes 1440.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no integrated GPUs, no local SSD storage, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached volumes and services.

Benchmark results place the c3d-standard-360 in the top 10% tier for heavily threaded computing and aggregate memory throughput. It achieved a multi-core score of 554304.29 in stress-ng and 157237.28 in PassMark CPU, bolstered by strong extended instruction execution (377497.22) and encryption throughput (418924.83). Large-block memory tests measured 697.13 GB/sec for uncached reads and 336.59 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance remains competitive, recording 2010.0 in Geekbench single-core and 3072.07 in stress-ng. Software compilation (70813.0) and ray tracing (249255.0) also scored in the top tier.

Real-world application tests highlight substantial capacity for data services and network serving. The instance sustained 414.29 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 160.75 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. CPU-based LLM inference demonstrated high prompt processing rates, reaching 4070.35 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 40.12 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. Text generation on the 70B model reached 6.15 tokens per second.

The primary operational tradeoff is the total absence of local NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies on network-attached persistent storage. The c3d-standard-360 is optimized for compute-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory databases, large-scale software builds, batch analytics, and centralized web traffic routing.
